Subject: Product title & training license — order form redlines

Hi Connor / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and procurement teams reviewed the draft order form and attached a set of redlines (see ACME_Redlines_v1.pdf). The key items they flagged:

- Output ownership: they want explicit assignment of productized output title when the customer provides datasets for fine-tuning.
- Training / model retrain: they requested an opt-out that prevents Redwood from using customer data for future model training, including derivative improvements.
- Feedback license: they want a narrow feedback license limited to debugging and service improvements, not model training.
- Telemetry / telemetry retention: brief asks on how telemetry used for productization is retained.

Can you propose language we could use in the order form (or alternative MSA exhibit) to accommodate a customer-first path while preserving Redwood's ability to operate and improve the hosted service? Procurement asked for a short MA Plan (milestones + owner + signoff) so we can accelerate the procurement cycle.

Attached: ACME_Redlines_v1.pdf (redlines from Acme legal)

Subject: Re: Product title & training license — order form redlines

Jordan — thanks for sending this over and for the clear summary. Quick read-through from my side and a suggested way forward so we can keep procurement moving: 

1) Two-path approach for output/training:
   - Option A (Enterprise Preferred): Customer retains title to "Customer-Provided Models and Derivatives" and Redwood receives a limited, non-exclusive license to use outputs for service delivery and immediate debugging; training on customer artifacts requires an explicit opt-in executed via the order form (checkbox + effective date).
   - Option B (Standard): Redwood retains operational rights to use aggregated telemetry and non-identifiable outputs for product improvement, with an explicit assurance that customer-specific datasets won't be used to update public models without opt-in.

2) Suggested clause placement: keep the high-level commitments in the Order Form (checkbox selection) and put the mechanics (definitions, evidence, auditability) in an MSA exhibit so legal signoff is faster and procurement has a single-page MA Plan.

3) Feedback license: propose narrower drafting — "Redwood may use Customer Feedback for the limited purposes of troubleshooting, improving the services used by the Customer, and addressing security/stability issues; Customer data used under this paragraph will not be included in training datasets for public models without separate written consent."

4) Telemetry: suggest a 90-day retention baseline for session telemetry used for operational debugging; anything longer should be opt-in and documented.

Ben, Laura — tagging you for redline language. If you can draft two short clause variants (Option A / Option B) I will push them to Jordan and prepare a one-page MA Plan with owners and timelines (legal review, procurement signoff, CSM acceptance). Jordan — would procurement be comfortable with a 3-step MA Plan: (1) clause selection (this week), (2) legal signoff on exhibit (3–5 business days), (3) procurement release & PO?

Connor O'Brien
Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed clause text for Acme — Option A / Option B (draft)

Connor / Laura — attaching two short clause drafts and a one-paragraph redline note for legal: proposed_clauses_20250914.docx. High level:

- Option A (Customer title + opt-in training):
  "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, limited license to use Customer Outputs solely to provide the Services to Customer, to troubleshoot and resolve incidents affecting Customer, and to perform service-specific improvement activities for Customer's account. Use of Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train or otherwise improve models that are made generally available outside Customer's environment requires the Customer's prior written opt-in via the Order Form."

- Option B (Operational improvements allowed):
  "Customer acknowledges Redwood may use aggregated and de-identified telemetry and non-identifiable Outputs to improve and operate the Services. Redwood will not use Customer-specific training datasets to update public models without Customer's prior written consent."

Also included a short exhibit template covering definitions ("Customer Data", "Customer Outputs", "Training Use", "Telemetry") and an MA Plan stub with owners: Connor (Commercial), Laura (Legal), Ben (Product/Eng), Jordan (Acme legal), Procurement (Acme).

Attachment: proposed_clauses_20250914.docx
